固定安装包下载 上传设置 `Content-Disposition: attachment`，`filename` 沿用经校验安装包的 basename，保留完整版本、平台和架构。固定 `dsh-latest-*` URL 与 nightly/stable 升级通道独立，不另加命名后缀。发布后需验证 CDN 响应头透传及浏览器保存文件名。 固定安装包下载在仓库根目录使用 `pnpm run upload:latest:mac:arm64`、`pnpm run upload:latest:mac:x64` 或 `pnpm run upload:latest:win:x64`。它们把已完成目标的 DMG 或 EXE 上传到 `desktop/dsh-latest-macos-arm64.dmg`、`desktop/dsh-latest-macos-x64.dmg` 或 `desktop/dsh-latest-windows-x64.exe`。生产 URL 以 `https://download.deepseek.com/` 开头；测试 URL 使用 `DOWNLOAD_TEST_ORIGIN`。两个部署环境均复用目标 dotenv 中的部署、bucket 和凭据、全部常规发布校验以及下述上传审计。每个命令覆盖一个固定对象，不发布更新清单、blockmap 或发布标签。测试固定下载在测试 bucket 中跨发布 ID 共享；包内更新 URL 仍要求原有发布 ID。发布由操作人员显式执行，也允许预发布版本。生产命令随后提交一次 EdgeOne URL 缓存清除任务并报告任务 ID，不查询或等待缓存清除完成。测试上传仍由部署基础设施管理缓存策略。本地回环测试覆盖上传行为；真实 COS 和 CDN 验收由发布操作人员负责。 生产固定下载要求在目标 dotenv 中配置 `DOWNLOAD_PROD_EO_ZONE_ID`，且既有 `DOWNLOAD_PROD_COS_SECRET_ID` / `DOWNLOAD_PROD_COS_SECRET_KEY` 身份具备对应站点的 `teo:CreatePurgeTask` 权限。发布操作人员须在使用前确认该权限；无需新增 CI Secret。上传前解析必需配置。提交请求超时为 30 秒，不自动重试。 命令报告提交已接受，不代表缓存清除已完成。EO 结果输出到控制台，不另建刷新记录文件；既有上传审计仅记录 COS 写入。提交被拒绝或未确认时，命令以失败状态退出，已上传安装包保持发布。连接中断或未收到响应时，先检查 EO 任务历史再重新提交。使用 `pnpm run purge:latest ` 可只提交刷新，无需上传；需要生产配置和凭据，无需本地安装包。DPAPI 用户复用原凭据启动器，在 `-Upload -Latest` 命令上添加 `-PurgeOnly`。按目标串行执行上传和单独刷新。[CI 发布工作流](ci/README.zh.md#recovery-and-records)使用独立的官网上传和刷新观察 job。 ## 上传凭据 Windows 操作人员可以在仓库外保存 CLIXML 对象，其中 `SecretId` 和 `SecretKey` 是经 DPAPI 加密的 SecureString 字段。[凭据启动器](../scripts/upload-with-credentials.ps1)要求显式提供 `-CredentialFile` 和 `-Environment production` 或 `test`；不指定 `-Upload` 时，只验证解密以及向本地 Node 子进程注入凭据，不发起网络请求。它要求 `PATH` 中有 Node，并使用加密该文件时的 Windows 用户和机器。明文、空字段及纯空白字段都会失败。父进程环境保持不变；子进程先清除无关密钥与 Node 预加载选项，再仅接收所选 COS 凭据对。原始子进程 stderr 不会显示，stdout 中的凭据值会被遮盖。此检查不能证明 COS 授权有效。显式上传还要求 `-Upload -Target -Bucket ` 及下述常规发布完成前提；真实云端上传仍需发布操作人员验收。在该上传调用中添加 `-Latest`，即可替换固定安装包，而不发布更新清单或发布标签。仅提交缓存刷新时，在 `-Upload -Latest -Environment production` 上添加 `-PurgeOnly`。部署环境和 bucket 仍须匹配 dotenv，但不读取安装包产物。此启动器支持长期密钥，不支持 STS 凭据。显式上传要求所选部署环境和 bucket 与目标 dotenv 文件及已完成的打包记录一致，才会发起网络写入；即使 dotenv 文件含有其他 COS 密钥，也使用 DPAPI 凭据对。 ## 上传审计与恢复 test 与 production 的 `upload:*` 上传在发布前置检查通过后，分别保留新的 `.desktop-build/upload-records/--*` 目录。`plan.json` 记录目标、版本、每个文件的大小/SHA-512 和发布的 YAML 字节；刷盘的 `events.jsonl` 记录 PUT 意图及可用的响应状态/请求 ID；`result.json` 记录完成结果或最后失败阶段。缺少最终结果表示中断或存储不可用，不表示成功。不记录凭据值、认证头或原始 SDK 错误。审计写入失败即停止后续 PUT。每个对象都以一次流式腾讯 COS PUT 上传，并携带显式长度与 Content-MD5；COS SDK 仅在请求体不是流时才会重发请求，上传器自身也不重试。保留部分记录，检查远端状态后再执行下一次操作：超时或回执写入失败不能证明对象未存储。这些记录仅在本地，不防篡改，也不会自动备份；每次发布应将它们与构建证据一同归档到受控存储。公网 CDN 回读仍是单独的发布验收，上传结果明确标记为 `not-performed`。 ## 开发备注 无。

# Desktop local verification English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Local download and mandatory-dialog evidence is separate from production backend integration, visual acceptance, and installed-application upgrades. Run the command in the [Desktop README](../README.md) to produce a fresh isolated report. Installed qualification can opt into `DSH_DESKTOP_UPDATE_JOURNAL_DIR`, an absolute directory outside the installation tree that both versions retain. Each main process flushes a separate JSONL file with its installed version, state transitions, and manual-operation milestones. Raw diagnostics and request data are excluded; storage errors propagate. The [journal decision](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-09-14-desktop-installed-update-journal.md) defines evidence limits. Unit and main-entry tests cover the journal; a signed installed upgrade is still unverified. ## Table of Contents - [Fault-report verification](#verification-diagnostics) - [Update dialog themes](#verification-theme) - [Native overlay visibility](#verification-overlay) - [Evidence](#verification-evidence) - [Manual walkthrough](#verification-interactive) - [Open verification](#verification-open) ## Fault-report verification See [recovery and diagnostics](../docs/diagnostics/README.md) for product behavior and limitations. Use a disposable profile and separate Electron `userData` with the actual packaged client. Construct a minimal local bundle with `package.json`, `dsh.bundle.patch` pointing to `cordis.patch.yml`, and an optional plugin module; archive it as a local `.tgz`. These packages deliberately break the application and must not be published or installed in a daily profile. Exercise import and plugin-initialization exceptions, an asynchronous exception after `appReady`, and a nonzero Host exit. A patch disabling the `agent`, `session`, `llm`, and `tools` providers exercises missing-service diagnostics. To check cross-restart history, select that bundle through `pluginManager`, then restart the same profile. Runtime scenarios require observing actual client readiness; `appReady` alone does not establish that the window is visible. Check the original error and cause or exit code, operation and Host run IDs across restart, report-collection completion and omissions, file retrieval from the native dialog, and startup after plugin recovery. Record the package version and source commit; successful package generation or a management result alone does not establish client functionality. Restore protocol associations and stop test processes afterward. For resource checks, use large sparse history files, unrelated files, dense records, and malformed or unfinished lines. Measure setup separately from collection in fresh processes, recording actual bytes read, output size, time, and peak memory. To check Worker cancellation, a test-only module hook can hold an asynchronous file open after writing an entry marker. Confirm that marker, observe Worker exit after the deadline, and compare the basic report bytes. This does not reproduce a kernel-hung system call or establish packaged-client behavior. ## Update dialog themes After `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run build`, run the real Electron palette fixture on macOS: ```sh apps/desktop/.desktop-build/targets/mac-arm64/electron/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron apps/desktop/tests/fixtures/update-theme.mjs ``` The fixture creates a private profile, loads the production shell HTML, sandboxed preloads, renderer scripts, and bundled design tokens, and substitutes only fixed IPC status responses. Its 12 cases cover ordinary and mandatory documents starting in light/dark mode, switching while open, and following system appearance. It checks transparent document backgrounds, surface/text/button/mask colors, the code/address surface, the dark-only 1 CSS px inset outline, and the ordinary close icon, then writes four screenshots and `result.json` to `.desktop-build/qualification/update-theme-*`. It does not start a Host, download updates, run an installer, or qualify Windows native rendering. The first-close notice shares the ordinary document's CSS and theme script. ## Native overlay visibility On macOS, reuse the cached Electron runtime after compiling the Desktop Host sources: ```sh pnpm exec tsc -b apps/desktop/tsconfig.host.json apps/desktop/.desktop-build/targets/mac-arm64/electron/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron apps/desktop/tests/fixtures/update-overlay-visibility.mjs ``` The fixture owns a unique profile and writes `result.json` under `.desktop-build/qualification/update-overlay-*`. It checks visible and hidden owners, absence of native child windows, retention of a separate control window’s focus after owner visibility notifications, and view/input cleanup including owner destruction. It uses no network, product login, or dsh Host. It qualifies the in-window carrier, not the full first-login or installation flow. ## Manual walkthrough For actual installation, publication after startup, failure/retry, and restart evidence, use the [installed-update operator checklist](installed-update/README.md). The interactive runner below intercepts installation and is a different qualification. With Host, client, and Desktop artifacts built, run `node --import tsx apps/desktop/scripts/test-workspace-updates.ts --interactive` from the repository root on Windows. The actual workspace stays open with a separate control window. Its menus select ordinary or mandatory updates, hold and release downloads, inject download failures, and queue or clear test tasks. Select a failure before starting the download. After installation approval and task shutdown, a fixture message reports the intercepted installer call; acknowledging it ends the walkthrough. Closing the control window also exits. Each run owns a private profile and loopback server; payloads are not installers. Restart the command for a fresh round. Omitting `--interactive` runs the automated scenarios with their 120-second deadline and automatic exit; interactive downloads have a ten-minute network deadline. After building Desktop, `node apps/desktop/scripts/test-update-channels.mjs` checks the pinned Electron updater against loopback feeds and downloaded inert files. It verifies channel filenames, downgrade prohibition, rollout eligibility, and retirement of actual download caches and stale confirmations after channel switching; on macOS it also closes the updater-created local handoff server. Windows pull-request CI runs this check after the blocking build. No installer, Host or remote publication runs. This qualification does not replace signed installed-app testing on Windows and macOS. ## Evidence The local command builds Desktop and executes Electron 44 with the actual HTTP updater, policy client, sandboxed preload, and mandatory renderer. It records each scenario and preserves its report under `.desktop-build/qualification/local-updater-*`. The installer call, external browser, and clipboard are observation substitutes; downloaded bytes are not an executable installer. Packaging supervision fixtures control their Git metadata and use real file hashes with inert child processes. Git-head and worktree changes still refuse packaging; concurrent tests cannot change the fixture’s recorded Git inputs. | Layer | Observed result | |---|---| | Ordinary updater | Same/older-version rejection, user-authorized full download, SHA-512 rejection, interrupted transfer, stalled-feed/download deadlines, explicit retry, coalesced requests, same-address feed replacement, readiness, and separate install handoff pass | | Mandatory policy | Flattened `40005`, exact release headers, guest requests, no-force validation, failure retention, interval/backoff, timeout, and disposal regressions pass | | Ordinary scheduling | Fake-clock regressions with the real coordinator verify bounded jitter/backoff, manual joins, success reset, no automatic download retry, wall-clock independence, and disposal. Main-entry tests verify focus/resume throttling, immediate explicit checks, and quit cleanup | | Actual mandatory window | Text-only server content, an embedded Windows shell frame with no additional native window and an enabled main window, Escape blocking, direct download, same-modal task confirmation, deferral, recovery-only page actions, navigation/copy feedback, and fresh policy clearance pass; focused main-entry tests verify close-to-hide without quitting or stopping the Host, with policy retained | | Actual ordinary dialog | Isolated preload, 380px card, 24px corners, theme-resolved primary button, translucent backdrop without parent blur, Escape cancellation retaining readiness, and task-warning approval with recorded installation handoff pass | | Unlocked Windows interaction | OS-level clicks and screenshots of the actual mandatory renderer confirm Escape blocking, user-started download, readiness, red policy-error feedback, and modal clearance with the parent enabled again. A fixture-provided native task-warning dialog returns to readiness on deferral; task activity is simulated, not a full Host workload | | Main entry | A known block refuses plugin mutations and recovery without stopping the Host; fresh success closes the block; packaged policy ignores environment overrides; installer failure after a clean stop restores the Host before another confirmation and retains mandatory blocking | | Host task protection | The actual controller with substituted composition detects running agents, queued turns/steps, and global and agent jobs; API reads do not warn. Admission locking returns 503 for new requests, drains existing requests, and rechecks tasks; unlock restores admission | | Visible output | Chinese mandatory-dialog DOM expectation and ordinary update presentation expectation pass; account-row component tests cover progress and persistent retry | | Packaging configuration | Metadata embeds the configured application ID and policy; the built pre-pack hook rejects an HTTP policy origin without running packaging or upload | The focused dialog, main-entry, settings, and sidebar run passes 119 regression cases. Five carrier tests cover all statements, branches, functions, and lines of the shared update-status source. The real-Electron command passes 17 scenarios and captures ordinary-ready, task-warning, and mandatory-error dialogs. These isolated checks do not certify the complete workspace or a release. Full-repository gate results and environment limitations remain separate from this focused evidence. Chromium headless shell revision 1228 is installed in the ignored `.desktop-build/playwright` directory. The assembled settings and sidebar browser suites pass 18 cases. The [Desktop workspace browser scenario](../../web/tests/desktop-updates.e2e.ts) passes both Chinese and English cases, captures six screenshots per locale, and verifies bottom-row placement, compact progress with duplicate-click rejection, a top-toggle badge, persistent red retry with error tooltip, and a separate ready action. It verifies queued turns/steps, a running model request, pending questions/approvals, global and agent jobs in running/stopping states, admission locking without cancellation, restored admission, and rejected inspection after Host disposal. Only model responses and human answers are substituted. Two independent invocations pass concurrently with private profiles and session data; all owned agents, jobs, and Hosts finish before a success report is written. The [Electron workspace runner](../scripts/test-workspace-updates.ts) executes a private copy of the compiled main entry with the real preload, workspace, and separate Host process. It acknowledges the first-run notice and drives renderer buttons through Electron input events and Chromium debugger input for the embedded Windows frame. The private application reuses the prepared target runtime resources. The recorded Windows run passes ten scenarios, covering menu feedback, download failure and retry, separate installation confirmation, real confirmation-time task creation, deferral, mandatory blocking, and actual Host teardown timeout. Both ordinary and mandatory failures restore a replacement Host and require fresh installation confirmation; recovery does not clear mandatory policy. Delivery uses a local server and installation is intercepted; these are not signed installed-app results. Unit regressions cover DN escaping, incomplete identities, and explicit or host-default Windows targets; removing the publisher configuration fails both metadata cases. This check does not download, install, or sign an artifact. The [signed-download runner](../scripts/test-signed-updates.mjs) connects real Electron HTTP, `NsisUpdater`, Windows Authenticode, and the built coordinator. The synthetic feed and test application adapter do not establish installed-version compatibility; no installer or Host starts. With an old installer and both original blockmaps, the same runner additionally verifies single-range and multipart-range reconstruction, missing-old-blockmap fallback, and rejected-range fallback. Reconstructed executables pass SHA-512 and Authenticode checks. Request records distinguish differential payload bytes from full downloads; a full fallback cannot satisfy a differential-success assertion. These loopback results do not certify CDN Range support or an installed application's cache. ## Open verification The following items are not passing evidence and must remain visible during review: - Electron `capturePage()` captures individual windows. Windows interactive observations include composed dialogs and native menu selection, but cross-platform Figma/layout acceptance and a complete recording remain unverified. The automated workspace runner invokes the menu handler directly. - The development launcher encounters a dangling optional Linux ARM64 dependency junction in this Windows checkout; the qualification runners link the existing dependency graph directly and do not validate that launcher's projection. - The fixture does not execute an installer, overwrite an installed application, or establish that a new version starts successfully. Signed Windows and macOS installed-version qualification remains required for release. - Two isolated Windows test installers pass signed-package inspection, including their embedded feed configuration. Installed startup, failure/retry, automatic restart, and data retention remain operator verification; file inspection does not certify a release. - Live policy origins, gateway behavior, rate limits, approved page origins, and deployed policy configuration are pending backend integration. Local responses are not proof of a live service. - Policy, updater feed, and updater download stalls reach their real deadlines and recover. Injected download-write `ENOSPC` is covered; actual volume exhaustion and installed-upgrade disk pressure remain unverified. Differential download and publisher rejection are verified through real Electron downloads, but not yet in a newly packaged application's installed-upgrade path. - Native clipboard writing passes on Windows. Default-browser launch is attempted, but destination verification stops because the automation tool cannot reliably identify the current URL. macOS browser and clipboard integration remain unverified. - Mandatory and ordinary failures use localized summaries and folded diagnostics; copy failure reveals a selectable address. Ordinary error tooltips show summaries rather than raw diagnostics. Installed Windows/macOS attention, notification permission, and focus-mode behavior remain unverified. - Full `doc-sync` encounters Windows file-symlink `EPERM` in the documentation-site test. This is not an updater failure and does not make the full documentation gate green.

--- description: "Configure and operate the Windows packaging runner, signing credentials, EV token and signature cache. Read the accepted isolation risks before running branch code or accessing the token. Hardware failures require operator inspection; packaging success does not establish installation or production readiness." --- # Windows signing and runner operations English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Configure and operate the Windows packaging runner, signing credentials, EV token and signature cache. Read the accepted isolation risks before running branch code or accessing the token. Hardware failures require operator inspection; packaging success does not establish installation or production readiness. ## Table of Contents - [Trust and isolation limits](#trust-and-isolation) - [Machine setup and runner startup](#machine-setup) - [Signing configuration](#signing-configuration) - [Signing and timestamp completion](#windows-ev-signing) - [Failure records and operator recovery](#failure-and-recovery) - [Signature cache and concurrent stages](#signature-cache) - [Verification limits](#verification) ## Trust and isolation limits The shared packaging runner assumes trusted internal-team code and operators. Under this assumption, credential and device isolation are deferred and the residual risk is accepted (tracked in #5973); signed/master-only access is not enforced. Unsigned mode skips signing-file loading but cannot prevent branch code running as the same Windows account from reading those files or accessing the token. SafeNet Single Logon may reuse authentication. Direct device calls can bypass the signing scripts and exhaust PIN retries; the persistent failure interlock only protects calls through those scripts. Cross-account token isolation and remaining retry counts are unverified. Reassess runner/account/device isolation before expanding access, executing untrusted contributions, changing runner sharing, or after suspicious activity. ## Machine setup and runner startup Use a runner-owned checkout and keep configuration, certificates and caches outside it. Registration and tool installation remain operator tasks. Packaging inputs and artifact retrieval are described in the [packaging guide](../packaging/README.md#windows-actions). Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/scripts/setup-windows-packaging.ps1 -Root ` to prepare private `packaging/{presets,secrets,certificates}` and `cache/windows-signatures` directories and copy templates without overwriting existing files. Add `-CheckOnly` to inspect without writes. Fill the [preset templates](../config/windows-packaging/test.env.example) and [signing template](../config/windows-packaging/windows-signing.env.example) on the machine. Run `start-windows-packaging-runner.ps1 -RunnerRoot -ConfigRoot /packaging -CheckOnly` from the same scripts directory to inspect PowerShell 7.6.6 under the runner's `tools` directory, Node, Python, Git, tar and Visual C++ tools; packaging `--check` performs the remaining toolchain validation. Omit `-CheckOnly` to start the existing runner with an explicit config root and scrubbed inherited environment. Registration and tool installation are separate; these scripts never create tokens, alter system security settings or clear signing failure records. Use the signing cache maintenance command below to migrate existing entries before changing the preset's cache path. ### Supervised startup For the complete registration, label, routing and approval sequence, start with [CI publication setup](../publishing/ci/README.md#setup-sequence). The task installer requires the Windows .NET Framework 4.5+ compiler at `%SystemRoot%/Microsoft.NET/Framework64/v4.0.30319/csc.exe`. It compiles a GUI executable into `runner/dsh-task/launcher.exe`; this executable starts PowerShell with no console and waits for it to exit. The output and errors of `run.ps1` itself go to uniquely named `launcher-*.out.log` and `launcher-*.err.log`; filenames include UTC time, PID and a random identifier. Launcher failures disable periodic starts, including failures before the retry budget can be read. Task result `2` indicates launcher failure; `3` means its error log could not be written; `4` means disabling the task also failed and an operator must disable it in Task Scheduler. After the direct child exits, output draining is limited to five seconds. A timeout returns `5` with a `launcher-*.drain.log` diagnostic: output may be incomplete, but periodic recovery continues within the existing restart budget. Descendant processes may outlive the exited runner; draining logs does not terminate them. The recorded stop target is the launcher process, so stop includes the launcher and its descendants. Normal runner output remains in `run-*.log`. Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/scripts/windows-runner-task.ps1 -Action install -RunnerRoot -ConfigRoot /packaging` as the runner's Windows user, using its installed PowerShell 7. The installer checks the environment and copies startup scripts into `runner/dsh-task`; registration, tools and secrets remain separate. It registers a disabled, limited-permission interactive Task Scheduler task without storing an account password. Task priority 4 gives the runner and its children normal CPU, I/O and memory priority; the scheduler default 7 lowers all three and slows dependency installation. Existing tasks retain their settings: while the runner is idle, stop, uninstall and reinstall the task before starting it again. For `-Action start` or `-Action status`, pass only `-RunnerRoot`; configuration and retry options apply only to installation. The task starts after this user's desktop login, including after reboot, and stops on logout. It does not provide unattended boot or unlock a signing Token. The task permits one instance and has no execution time limit. A repeating trigger checks every `-RestartMinutes` minutes (default `1`) and restarts an exited launcher, including an unexpected zero exit. The persisted budget permits the initial launch plus `-RestartCount` restarts (default `10`) between explicit starts. Every desktop login also consumes this budget; `status` shows the remaining launches. After the budget is exhausted, login alone cannot restart the runner. Starting an already running task does not reset the budget. Missing or invalid budget/configuration files disable automatic starts until repaired. GitHub's launcher owns runner updates; task recovery does not rerun a failed workflow or clear signing interlocks. After retries are exhausted, inspect `runner/dsh-task/run-*.log`, the runner's `_diag` logs and `status`, correct the cause, then run `start`. A running task alone does not prove connectivity: verify `Connected to GitHub` and `Listening for Jobs`, then verify assignment in Actions. Both `run-*.log` and `launcher-*.log` are retained for operator-managed cleanup. Before maintenance, pause new workflow dispatch and wait for the runner to become idle. `-Action stop` refuses an active worker for this runner, disables future starts and stops its task process tree; the local check cannot prevent a concurrent GitHub assignment. `-Action uninstall` requires a stopped, disabled task and retains registration, configuration and logs. Pulling repository changes does not update the installed copy. To upgrade it, record the original -ConfigRoot, optional -NetworkRoot and retry settings, then run `stop`, `uninstall`, `install` with those settings, and `start` from the updated checkout. Confirm listening and job assignment again. When migrating a manually launched runner, stop its existing launcher only after it is idle, then start the task; never run both launchers together. Operators can run `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/tests/windows-runner-task.ps1` on Windows to exercise installation, console-free initial launch and automatic recovery, duplicate-start prevention, stop, child-process teardown, containment of startup/logging failures and uninstall against an isolated fake runner. This opt-in test creates a temporary task and retains diagnostic files; it does not contact GitHub or access signing hardware. `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/tests/windows-runner-launcher.ps1` checks the GUI executable, child console absence, exit status, diagnostic output and bounded draining with an inherited writer without Task Scheduler; Windows CI runs it. Real-machine acceptance additionally checks an idle runner coming online without a visible Terminal window, an Actions job being assigned, and login after an operator-approved reboot. Signed packaging and logout/reboot acceptance require separate operator verification. ### Optional network dependency Without `runner-network.json` in `ConfigRoot`, startup retains its scrubbed direct-network behavior. To configure a network dependency, create that operator-owned JSON file outside the checkout with exactly `proxyUrl`, `noProxy`, `serviceName`, `probeUrl`, `attempts`, `timeoutSeconds` and `retrySeconds`. The first four fields are strings; the three budgets are integers from 1 through 60. Use an empty `proxyUrl` for direct access and an empty `serviceName` when no Windows service owns the dependency. URLs must use HTTP(S) without credentials, queries or fragments; the proxy URL cannot include a path. Startup applies `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` after environment scrubbing, then requires a successful Node HEAD probe before admitting the runner. Service readiness checks never start or stop a Windows service. For a dedicated child process, add `-NetworkRoot ` to task installation. That directory must contain `launch.json` with exactly an absolute `executable` filename, an `arguments` string array and an integer `restartDelaySeconds` from 1 through 3600. This mode requires `runner-network.json`; set its `serviceName` to empty. Give the child its own data directory, listener bindings and executable identity, distinct from applications managed by desktop software; separate ports alone do not prevent another manager from terminating a process by executable name. The scripts do not alter desktop network settings. Keep actual provider names, paths, addresses, ports and arguments in machine configuration, never in repository files or shared logs. Restrict access to both configuration directories to the runner operator. Installation starts the dependency for readiness checking and stops it before registering the task. While the runner lives, the supervisor restarts only an exited owned network process after the configured delay, including repeated launch failures; it does not restart the runner or retry jobs or signing. Exit, restart and launch-failure messages appear in `run-*.log`; provider output is discarded. Restart messages establish process creation, not network availability: confirm reconnection in runner logs. A live but unresponsive dependency requires operator diagnosis. The supervisor exclusively locks `NetworkRoot`, verifies PID, start time and executable before reclaiming a stale child, and stops its child when the runner exits. Unrecoverable supervision errors leave the active runner alive until it exits and report that recovery has stopped. Preserve `NetworkRoot` when reinstalling; pulling changes alone does not replace installed helpers. Windows CI runs `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/tests/windows-runner-network.ps1` and `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/tests/windows-runner-network-process.ps1` with isolated local fixtures. On a configured packaging machine, add `-CheckStartup` to the first command to verify network configuration after the actual startup environment scrub. These tests use no signing hardware or external network endpoints. ## Signing configuration The [machine preset configuration](../packaging/README.md#configuration-and-local-builds) selects public settings and the signing file. Without a preset, use the target dotenv file. Fill in `.env.windows` with `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_CER_FILE` (public EV leaf certificate), `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_SIGNTOOL` (SafeNet-compatible SignTool), `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_KEY_CONTAINER` (matching private-key container), and `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_TOKEN_PIN` (Token Password). The private key stays on the USB token; keep the certificate and local credential file out of Git. The PIN cannot contain `]`, a quote, or a line break because those characters delimit the SafeNet `/kc` value or its CMD argument. The CMD disables delayed expansion so a PIN containing `!` reaches SafeNet unchanged. Packaging withholds every `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_*` field from build and runtime-preparation subprocesses, gives signing preflight, the dedicated runtime signing stages and electron-builder only the four configured inputs, gives the signing CMD only the validated signing fields in an otherwise scrubbed environment, clears those fields before SignTool starts, and redacts SignTool diagnostics. SafeNet still requires the PIN in the SignTool process command line. The local `.env.windows` or machine-owned `secrets/windows-signing.env` stores the PIN in plaintext and needs restricted file access. CI reads the machine-owned file outside the checkout and retains it across jobs. Do not commit or share its contents or print credentials in logs. Configuration checks consume no token PIN attempts; signing still stops the batch on its first failure. Signed Windows configuration derives the updater's `publisherName` from the same public certificate's `CN`, `O`, and `C` attributes. Each must be present, nonempty, and single-valued. These identity attributes allow certificate renewal without pinning a leaf thumbprint. The installed application's `app-update.yml` carries the expected publisher; the downloaded feed does not choose it. Unsigned test builds omit updater configuration. See the [signature qualification record](../tests/README.md) for real-file verification and its limits. ## Signing and timestamp completion Follow the [version and build instructions](../packaging/README.md#release-versions) before starting a signed build. Configuration checks do not establish token authentication. Signed Windows builds run a supervised signing preflight before compilation or dependency preparation. Static configuration, certificate validity, audit storage, compiler availability and any retained signing interlock are checked without token access. The local .NET Framework C# compiler creates a small private probe; the production signer signs it once, and verification requires the configured certificate and a timestamp before building continues. The probe is never executed. The overall 60-second preflight deadline includes timestamp attempts; deadline expiry, hardware signing errors and verification failures stop the run without another hardware attempt. Success proves the current signing path works, not that the PIN was independently authenticated: SafeNet may reuse login state. Do not log out or repeat authentication to test the PIN. `--check`, preparation-only and `--unsigned` modes do not run this hardware preflight; unsigned artifacts remain ineligible for release upload. Automated regression tests use a fake signer; release operators qualify real hardware separately. Public identity queries require PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) on the build account’s `PATH`; an unavailable or failed query process stops signing with an unknown identity result. Before compiling the probe, a separate noninteractive process reads public keys from the fixed eToken CSP using `CRYPT_VERIFYCONTEXT | CRYPT_SILENT`. It receives the container name but no PIN or signing credentials, and has a 15-second deadline within the existing preflight deadline. Both RSA key slots must be read completely (an absent slot is allowed); at least one public key must match the configured certificate. Provider/container access failure, unsupported public reads, malformed output, timeout or mismatch stops before hardware signing. A container-access error does not establish that the device or container is absent. Public information can be cached by middleware: a match does not authenticate the device, validate the PIN or establish remaining retries. This path is covered by a simulated CSP; the installed SafeNet version still requires separate operator qualification. No failure automatically retries authentication or clears the existing interlock. Insert and unlock the token before packaging. The electron-builder hook passes each artifact to the CRLF `scripts/windows-sign.cmd`, which invokes the configured SignTool once with `/f`, SafeNet `/kc "[{{PIN}}]=container"`, `/csp "eToken Base Cryptographic Provider"`, a SHA-256 file digest, without a timestamp. The hook then completes a DigiCert SHA-256 RFC 3161 timestamp on isolated copies without signing credentials. The hook never substitutes electron-builder's bundled SignTool and never retries a failed signing request. Windows release packaging fails instead of emitting unsigned artifacts when the SignTool, certificate, container, PIN, token, or signature is unavailable. Timestamp completion retries only a normally exited timestamp command returning failure or warning, at most three times with one- and two-second delays. Each attempt starts from the same verified primary signature. Launch errors, uncertain termination and verification failures stop immediately. SignTool operates on short private paths; publication copies verified bytes to the target volume before atomic replacement. Final Windows trust, certificate, timestamp and normalized full-file equality are required. Exhaustion stops packaging and preserves evidence without another hardware call. See the [signature completion decision](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-17-windows-signature-completion.md). ## Failure records and operator recovery Treat `SignTool Error: No private key is available.` as a signing failure: stop all signing attempts and have the operator inspect the signing configuration and token state before continuing. The device-specific PIN retry limit and remaining attempts are unverified; do not probe them with authentication attempts. Do not retry packaging or signing probes after this error. The signer serializes token operations and rejects all queued tasks after the first failure. Windows package commands print `DESKTOP_PACKAGING_RECORD` with a unique directory under `.desktop-build/packaging-runs/`. Each run retains `run.json`, timestamped `events.jsonl`, redacted `stdout.log` and `stderr.log`, and `result.json`. A signing failure also writes `fatal.json` and notifies the parent through stderr; the supervisor immediately requests termination of its stage process tree and waits for exit. Failed stages cannot start subsequent stages or create a release completion record. Journal failures also stop the run. Termination errors remain failures and require operator inspection; a missing final record means completion was not established. Hardware signing requires a supervised run. Before invoking the command interpreter, the signer atomically acquires `%USERPROFILE%/.dsh-desktop-signing/attempt.json` and records the attempt. Only successful signing followed by verification of the configured primary signature releases that file; timestamps are completed afterward without hardware access. Failure, interruption, an existing interlock, or unavailable audit storage prevents further hardware access, including from another signer instance, process, or checkout under the same Windows account. There is no timed recovery or automatic retry. An administrator must inspect the retained evidence and token state before explicitly authorizing interlock recovery; logging into the token or replacing a PIN file does not clear it. The records distinguish signing intent, command-interpreter PID, and completion; they do not measure internal CSP/token authentication attempts. Command arguments, PINs, and credential environments are not recorded. Independent Windows accounts and unrelated signing programs are outside this interlock. ## Signature cache and concurrent stages Runtime signing shares complete signed files across the current Windows account's worktrees. `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_SIGNATURE_CACHE_DIR` in `.env.windows` selects an absolute fixed-drive directory; the default is `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh-desktop-signing\signature-cache\v1`. Cache directories must belong to the current account and exclude other ordinary accounts from their access permissions; linked paths are rejected. Entries identify the original bytes, public certificate and signing toolchain. Every restoration checks the digest, Windows trust, timestamp and certificate before replacing the unsigned file; invalid entries stop packaging without hardware fallback. Cache age alone does not trigger signing. The cache trusts programs running as the same account and does not defend against administrators. The [runtime signature cache decision](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-17-windows-runtime-signature-cache.md) owns qualification and design limits. Preflight, primary-runtime signing, application-runtime signing and artifact creation each hold the account's signing-stage lock until their supervised child processes settle. Other builds wait before entering those stages; compilation and preparation do not hold the lock. Runtime signing workers own their locks, so terminating only the outer packaging process does not unlock a surviving cache user. Migration and maintenance acquire the same lock; older or external signing commands do not participate and must be scheduled separately. Stage waiting is outside the preflight deadline. Closing the stage handle releases ordinary contention without removing the separate hardware-attempt interlock; a retained hardware failure still requires operator recovery. Cache-hit copying, hashing and per-file candidate trust checks run with `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_SIGNATURE_CACHE_CONCURRENCY` workers from `.env.windows` (default `4`, integer `1`–`8`). After all restores finish, bounded PowerShell batches verify every restored target's trust, timestamp and certificate before cache misses enter serial hardware signing. A restore failure stops new restores and drains active workers; a target-verification failure drains its inspection batch and prevents hardware signing. Runtime smoke checks and final integrity validation remain required. PE discovery reads every regular file's header with at most eight open files, rejects links and malformed Windows executables, and drains active reads and closes before reporting failure. Packaging records `windows:enumerate-code` and `windows:inspect-signatures` as nested phases of signing and artifact verification; their timings are included in the enclosing stages. Windows packaging reads `DSH_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_PACK_CONCURRENCY` from `.env.windows` or the selected preset: a positive integer, defaulting to `4`. Packaging batches first-party and vendor tarballs with bounded workers, then validates every payload and records publication order. After the complete build succeeds, tarball packing overlaps Electron and primary-runtime preparation in separate output directories. Both must finish successfully before runtime signing; preparation failure stops new packing commands and drains active processes before returning. Setting the limit to `1` selects serial tarball workers; standalone `release:pack` defaults to `1`. Each runtime stage writes `SIGNATURE_CACHE_SUMMARY` to stdout and its packaging journal, including the actual directory, policy identity, hit/miss counts, newly published and retained entries, signing requests, avoided signing requests and validation failures. Timings distinguish signing, trust verification of restored and newly signed files, and restoration; restoration includes its trust check and staging cleanup. These counters exclude preflight, final artifact signing and the outer runtime signature checks. Stage lock events record waiting separately. Concurrent timings sum per-file work rather than stage wall time. Use `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run cache:windows-signatures --usage` to inspect structurally complete-entry bytes and counts, or `--from ` to import an explicitly selected cache owned by the same account. Migration leaves the source unchanged, skips staging names, rejects corrupt entries and retains valid existing entries even when their timestamp bytes differ. `--clear` explicitly removes complete entries under the stage lock; no automatic capacity eviction runs. `--directory ` selects a maintenance destination without loading release credentials. Incomplete staging entries remain untouched and are counted separately; inspect them only after all builds have stopped. These commands never clear hardware failure evidence. Default storage is outside AppData so MSIX launcher virtualization does not split the account's cache; redirected overrides fail explicitly. ## Verification limits Signing performance evidence and replacement-runner retesting are owned by the [signing concurrency qualification](../tests/signing-concurrency/README.md). Update and installation evidence is owned by the [Desktop qualification record](../tests/README.md) and [installed-update procedure](../tests/installed-update/README.md). This document does not authorize PIN retries, automatic interlock deletion, device initialization or changes to the accepted isolation policy. For operator-approved concurrency experiments, run `node apps/desktop/tests/windows-signing-concurrency.perf.ts --execute --config-root --rounds 2`. Without `--execute`, it only prints usage. The default compares serial completion, two completion workers with one hardware request, and two concurrent hardware requests on six synthetic PE copies per batch. The second round reverses mode order. Add `--corpus ` to compare 1, 2 and 4 workers on real release files. The manifest is a nonempty JSON array of objects with an absolute `path` and its lowercase hexadecimal `sha256`. Preparation copies each pinned file, verifies its signature and removes any valid signature from the copy; invalid signatures or changed bytes stop preparation. Signature removal requires SignTool with `remove /s`; `--strip-tool ` overrides only that public preparation tool when the configured version lacks support. Hardware signing and timestamping still use the machine preset. Every batch uses fresh, byte-checked copies of the unsigned templates, preserving manifest order. `--pipeline-control` with a corpus instead runs four completion workers with one hardware request. Original files and release caches remain unchanged. The experiment uses the machine test preset, checks public identity, holds the account signing-stage lock and retains one hardware-attempt interlock per batch. The first failure stops dispatch and drains issued work; up to four hardware calls may already be in flight. Only complete signature, timestamp and file verification permits normal interlock release. Files are never executed. Records remain under `.desktop-build/qualification/signing-concurrency`, including batch and per-file elapsed times, batch endpoint host CPU counters, free memory and driver-process memory samples. These memory samples exclude child processes and do not establish peak memory. Timings exclude input preparation, lock waiting and package assembly. Replaying ready-made artifacts also excludes build dependencies between them; the experiment does not enable production concurrency or establish full-release performance. ## Dev Note None.

checkout，并将配置、证书和缓存放在其外部。注册和工具安装由操作者负责。打包输入与产物获取见[打包指南](../packaging/README.zh.md#windows-actions)。 运行 `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/scripts/setup-windows-packaging.ps1 -Root ` 创建私有 `packaging/{presets,secrets,certificates}` 和 `cache/windows-signatures` 目录并复制模板，不覆盖现有文件。添加 `-CheckOnly` 只检查不写入。在机器上填写 [preset 模板](../config/windows-packaging/test.env.example)和[签名模板](../config/windows-packaging/windows-signing.env.example)。从同一 scripts 目录运行 `start-windows-packaging-runner.ps1 -RunnerRoot -ConfigRoot /packaging -CheckOnly`，检查 runner 的 `tools` 目录下 PowerShell 7.6.6、Node、Python、Git、tar 和 Visual C++ 工具；打包 `--check` 完成其余工具链检查。省略 `-CheckOnly`，以显式配置目录和清理后的继承环境启动现有 runner。注册和工具安装单独进行；这些脚本不创建 token、不改系统安全设置、不清除签名失败记录。修改 preset 缓存路径前，使用下文签名缓存维护命令迁移已有条目。 ### 受监督启动 完整的注册、标签、路由和审批配置顺序见 [CI 发布配置](../publishing/ci/README.zh.md#setup-sequence)。任务安装器需要 Windows .NET Framework 4.5+ 编译器，路径为 `launcher-*.err.log`，文件名包含 UTC 时间、PID 和随机标识。启动器失败时禁用周期启动，包括尚未读取重试预算时发生的失败。任务结果 `2` 表示启动器失败，`3` 表示无法写入错误日志，`4` 表示禁用任务也失败，需要操作者在计划任务中手动禁用。直接子进程退出后，最多等待五秒排空输出；超时返回 `5`，将诊断写入 `launcher-*.drain.log`：输出可能不完整，但周期恢复仍受原有重试预算约束。后代进程可能在 runner 退出后继续运行；日志排空不会终止它们。记录的停止目标是启动器进程，因此 stop 覆盖启动器及其后代。正常 runner 输出仍保存在 `run-*.log`。 以 runner 的 Windows 用户运行 `pwsh -NoProfile -File apps/desktop/scripts/windows-runner-task.ps1 -Action install -RunnerRoot -ConfigRoot /packaging`，使用该机器安装的 PowerShell 7。安装器检查环境，并将启动脚本复制到 `runner/dsh-task`；注册、工具和凭据仍单独管理。它注册一个初始禁用、权限受限的交互式计划任务，不保存账户密码。任务优先级 4 让 runner 及子进程使用普通 CPU、I/O 和内存优先级；计划任务默认值 7 会降低三者的优先级，使依赖安装变慢。已有任务保留原设置：在 runner 空闲时停止、卸载并重新安装任务，再启动。执行 `-Action start` 或 `-Action status` 时只传 `-RunnerRoot`；配置目录及重试选项仅适用于安装。任务在该用户登录桌面后启动，重启后也需要登录，注销时停止。它不提供无人值守开机，也不解锁签名 Token。 任务只允许一个实例，且没有执行时限。周期触发器每隔 `-RestartMinutes` 分钟（默认 `1`）检查一次，并恢复已退出的启动器，包括意外的零退出码。持久预算允许首次启动及 `-RestartCount` 次重启（默认 `10`），直到再次显式启动。每次桌面登录也会消耗预算，`status` 显示剩余启动次数；预算耗尽后，仅登录不能重启 runner。对正在运行的任务执行 start 不会重置预算。预算或配置文件缺失、无效时，自动启动会禁用，需修复后恢复。GitHub 启动器负责 runner 更新；任务恢复不会重跑失败的 `sha256`。准备阶段复制哈希固定的文件，验证签名并仅移除副本上的有效签名；签名无效或字节变化会中止准备。移除签名要求 SignTool 支持 `remove /s`；配置中的版本不支持时，可用 `--strip-tool ` 仅覆盖这个公开准备工具。硬件签名和时间戳仍使用机器 preset。每批使用经过字节比对的全新无签名模板副本，保持清单顺序。配合语料使用 `--pipeline-control` 时，改为四个完成任务共用一个硬件请求。原文件和发布缓存保持不变。 实验读取机器 test preset，核对公开身份，持有账户签名阶段锁，每批保留一条硬件尝试保护记录。首错停止派发并排空已发出的工作；最多可能已有四条硬件请求在途。只有全部签名、时间戳和文件验证成功才正常释放保护记录。文件从不执行。记录保留在 `.desktop-build/qualification/signing-concurrency`，包含整批及单文件耗时、批次起止时的主机 CPU 计数、可用内存和驱动进程内存采样。内存采样不含子进程，不能用于确定峰值内存。计时不含输入准备、等锁和包组装。重放现成产物还排除了它们之间的构建依赖；实验不启用生产并发，也不代表完整发布性能。 ## 开发备注 无。

# Alibaba Cloud deployment

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Deploy the account, organization and project service on a dedicated ECS instance. Native DSH sessions and local previews remain on their originating computers. Do not expose one DSH owner's Web profile as a multi-user server.

Use Ubuntu 24.04, Docker Engine and Compose v2. From `services/ipollowork`, create a private `.env` with these values and a URL-safe random database password. When migrating, preserve the existing authentication secret, settings and database.

~~~dotenv
SERVICE_DOMAIN=cloud.ipollo.net
SERVICE_ORIGIN=https://cloud.ipollo.net
PUBLICATION_DOMAIN=publish.ipollo.net
PUBLICATION_ORIGIN=https://publish.ipollo.net
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-random-secret
OSS_RAM_ROLE=ipollowork-storage
OSS_INTERNAL=true
~~~

Attach an ECS role using `oss-role-trust.json` and `oss-role-policy.json`. The policy grants object read, write and delete only in the named publication Bucket; replace that resource for another deployment. Set region and Bucket in the service's central OSS settings. The official SDK retrieves and renews temporary credentials through IMDSv2; no long-lived AccessKey is required. Leave `OSS_RAM_ROLE` empty to use stored keys outside ECS.

~~~sh
chmod 600 .env
docker compose -p ipollowork -f compose.yml -f deploy/compose.production.yml up -d --build
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:4785/api/health
~~~

After checking local health, point the domain at the ECS public IP. The proxy opens HTTP and HTTPS and manages the certificate. The service port is loopback-only and PostgreSQL has no published port. `PROXY_IP` and `SERVICE_SUBNET` override the private Compose network; the IP must belong to that subnet. The proxy replaces the client-IP header and leaves request-path logging disabled. Native share WebSockets use the same hostname.

Point the publication domain at the same IP. It must differ from the account-service origin: it serves only published files, while account APIs remain on the service domain. Draft files cannot be browsed. A complete publication preserves relative resource paths and supports HTML, CSS, JavaScript and byte-range media reads; uploaded objects remain private in OSS.

Verify HTTPS health, existing-account login, organization access and an authorized OSS upload/download before changing clients' `accountOrigin`. Preserve the old DNS value for rollback. See [storage](../docs/storage.md) for migration and backup. Database backups use a separate destination; the publication Bucket holds explicitly published content.

Back up PostgreSQL, the authentication secret and settings before replacing containers. Reuse the same Compose project name and all data/certificate volumes. Never run `down -v` on an existing installation. Roll application code back only when it supports the installed database version.

For the 100-user trial, see [capacity and verified limits](../docs/capacity.md). The optional `-f deploy/compose.beta-2c4g.yml` adds a bounded single-host memory budget; adding it to an existing deployment restarts PostgreSQL, so rehearse it with backups and a maintenance window. `/api/health` checks process liveness, `/api/ready` checks database readiness. The application drains requests before shutdown; the Compose grace period is 40 seconds. External uptime monitoring and off-host backups are still required.

# 阿里云部署

[English](README.md) | 中文

在独立 ECS 实例上部署账号、组织和项目服务。原生 DSH 会话和本地预览保留在各自的电脑上。不要把单个 DSH 用户的 Web 配置作为多人服务器开放。

使用 Ubuntu 24.04、Docker Engine 和 Compose v2。在 `services/ipollowork` 中创建私有 `.env`，填写以下配置，并生成仅含 URL 安全字符的随机数据库密码。迁移时保留原有身份验证密钥、设置和数据库。

~~~dotenv
SERVICE_DOMAIN=cloud.ipollo.net
SERVICE_ORIGIN=https://cloud.ipollo.net
PUBLICATION_DOMAIN=publish.ipollo.net
PUBLICATION_ORIGIN=https://publish.ipollo.net
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-random-secret
OSS_RAM_ROLE=ipollowork-storage
OSS_INTERNAL=true
~~~

使用 `oss-role-trust.json` 和 `oss-role-policy.json` 创建并绑定 ECS 角色。策略仅允许读写和删除指定发布 Bucket 内的对象；其他部署需替换资源名称。在服务的统一 OSS 设置中填写地域和 Bucket。官方 SDK 通过 IMDSv2 获取并续期临时凭证，无需长期 AccessKey。在 ECS 之外使用已保存的密钥时，将 `OSS_RAM_ROLE` 留空。

~~~sh
chmod 600 .env
docker compose -p ipollowork -f compose.yml -f deploy/compose.production.yml up -d --build
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:4785/api/health
~~~

本地健康检查通过后，将域名指向 ECS 公网 IP。代理开放 HTTP 和 HTTPS 并管理证书。服务端口仅绑定回环地址，PostgreSQL 不发布端口。`PROXY_IP` 和 `SERVICE_SUBNET` 可覆盖 Compose 私有网络；IP 必须位于该网段内。代理覆盖客户端 IP 请求头，不启用请求路径日志。原生分享 WebSocket 使用同一域名。

将发布域名指向同一个 IP。它必须与账号服务来源不同：发布域名只提供已发布的文件，账号接口仍位于服务域名。草稿文件不能被浏览。完整发布保留资源相对路径，支持 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 和媒体文件的分段读取；OSS 中的对象仍保持私有。

修改客户端 `accountOrigin` 前，验证 HTTPS 健康检查、原有账号登录、组织访问和授权 OSS 上传下载。保留旧 DNS 值以便回退。迁移和备份参见[存储](../docs/storage.md)。数据库备份使用独立目的地；发布 Bucket 只保存明确发布的内容。

替换容器前，备份 PostgreSQL、身份验证密钥和设置。重复部署时沿用同一 Compose 项目名及所有数据和证书卷。已有部署不得执行 `down -v`。只有兼容已安装数据库版本的应用代码才可回退。

百人内测的配置与已验证边界见[容量说明](../docs/capacity.zh.md)。可选的 `-f deploy/compose.beta-2c4g.yml` 增加同机内存预算；应用到已有部署会重启 PostgreSQL，应在备份后安排维护窗口并先演练。`/api/health` 检查进程存活，`/api/ready` 检查数据库可用性。应用停机前会排空请求，Compose 留有 40 秒宽限期。仍需站外可用性监测和异机备份。

--- description: "Use this reference when recovering Desktop failures or collecting reports; it explains report contents, operation history, and shutdown limits." --- # Desktop recovery and diagnostics English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary This reference describes Desktop native failure recovery, diagnostic reports, recent plugin operation records, and collection and shutdown limits. ## Table of Contents - [Recover from a failure](#recovery) - [Report contents](#report-contents) - [Recent operation records](#operation-records) - [Collection and shutdown](#collection-and-shutdown) ## Recover from a failure Fatal main-window creation, main-document loading, preload, renderer, Web initialization, or backend failures open one native recovery dialog per application process. It shows a bounded tail of the first error, notes any truncation, and offers “Exit”, “Restart”, “Disable third-party plugins, back up profile patch, and restart”, and “Get diagnostic report” while report writing is pending or after it succeeds. Startup failures retain the Web loading page and spinner; runtime failures retain the current page. Expected shutdowns, cancelled navigation, and ordinary requests do not trigger recovery. The shared Web plugin manager reports package-operation errors; Host startup failures after plugin changes enter native recovery. There is no startup timeout heuristic. A listener failure containing `listen EADDRINUSE` replaces the diagnostics and reinstall advice with guidance to quit other running DSH instances, and offers “Exit”, “Restart”, and “Get diagnostic report” while report writing is pending or after it succeeds. Recovery uses the last confirmed Desktop language from the local cache before Host settings are available; an absent or invalid cache falls back to system languages. Recovery waits for Host shutdown before changing plugin activation. The native recovery action calls the shared app-boot recovery function under the profile transaction lock. It disables third-party bundles and renames the profile’s `cordis.patch.yml` to `cordis.patch.yml.bak-` (with an ordinal on collisions) without parsing it; the next startup creates an empty patch. Installed packages and earlier backups remain. The home-level patch is unchanged. The Electron console records the backup path (or its absence) and the unchanged home-level patch. Invalid profile data, rename failures, or write failures are reported as recovery-operation errors; completed changes remain, and Desktop does not restart as though recovery succeeded. Desktop has no profile-reset action or emergency HTML document. ## Report contents Native dialog details include at most 1,200 UTF-16 code units and eight diagnostic lines, plus the crash report path or its pending/unavailable status. Retrieving a pending or unavailable report preserves any recovery-operation failure headline and details. Configuration paths and startup entries precede the composition inventory so plugin rows cannot displace them when output is truncated. Host error diagnostics retain only the last 64 Ki characters written to stderr. Earlier output is discarded so a long-running Host does not grow the shell’s diagnostic buffer indefinitely. Before the first fatal dialog opens, Electron writes a crash report to the platform logs directory (`app.getPath('logs')`: `~/Library/Logs/iPolloWork` on macOS, `logs` under the application’s `userData` directory on Windows and Linux), waiting at most one second for the write; a slow or failed write shows the dialog with an explicit pending or unavailable status. Get diagnostic report checks the same write and reveals a saved file in the system file manager without restarting or stopping the Host; a write that completes after the initial deadline remains available. The user attaches that file to a support ticket. The attachment contains the original failure; later recovery-operation errors remain in the dialog and require a separate screenshot. Retrieving a saved report shows its sharing or reveal-failure heading while retaining the recovery error details. If writing fails, the dialog hides Get diagnostic report and suggests providing a screenshot. The file `crash--.log` records the source (`host` for a Host exit, `web-boot` for a renderer boot failure, `renderer` for a renderer or document failure, `main` for a shell error), whether the backend had reached ready, application and runtime versions, the error with its enumerable properties and cause chain (cut at 256 KiB), the Host’s own error and explicitly selected startup metadata (at most 64 Ki characters, including a truncation notice; startup errors reserve space for metadata by limiting the original error and startup-entry details to 8 Ki characters each, with explicit truncation notices) when the Host reported a startup failure over IPC before exiting, and the primary window’s recent error-level console output (at most 64 KiB). A Host exit report therefore contains the retained stderr tail, which may include plugin output. A fatal failure during shutdown writes a report without opening a dialog. Files are owner-only where the platform supports it; startup keeps the ten newest reports and removes older ones without touching other files in the directory. ## Recent operation records Operation records and the application single-instance lock are isolated by `userData`; the shared platform logs directory does not store operation records. The reader only reads the two operation files under `userData/plugin-operations`. Repairing an unfinished append preserves complete lines in the current segment and the previous segment. Version-exemption changes reuse the bundle enable/disable record fields. When the exemption and installed versions match, the record cannot distinguish an exemption change from a bundle toggle. Host `transportDropped` is a lower bound as of the last successful delivery; Desktop rejects malformed or mismatched-run records without adding them to that counter. The journal retains two 256 KiB segments, accepts records up to 4 KiB, and bounds queued writes to 64 KiB. Exit, recovery restart and installer preparation wait at most 500 ms for queued writes; a timeout disables further writes and later drains return immediately without another wait, while an already-issued OS request may still settle. Records cover manager operations observed after Host startup, not direct CLI commands or manual file changes. Package-manager output remains in its existing detailed logs and is not copied into this summary. Missing records, a start without an end, and damaged history do not establish a successful operation. This collection does not diagnose kernel hangs, OOM or native crashes. Persistence failures also disable the writer for the rest of this shell lifetime, including after recovery or installer failure. This bounds repeated failing I/O and avoids appending behind an uncertain partial write. Restarting the application creates a new writer. Omission and repair counters cover only the current shell lifetime. Retained segments provide a larger local troubleshooting window than the deliberately smaller report attachment. ## Collection and shutdown After saving the basic report, the shell attempts to append recent plugin-management records in an isolated Worker packaged as `lib/operation-report-worker.js` inside `app.asar`. The completion marker and omission counters distinguish a finished collection from missing or partial material. The Host announces its run ID before profile loading; reported Host errors carry that ID as `hostRunId`, matching operation records from the same lifetime. Failure before this announcement leaves the run identity unknown. Recent operations are context, not proof of cause. Collection reads only two owned files under `userData/plugin-operations`, at most 64 KiB and 100 records; the complete appended section is limited to 64 KiB. The 500 ms collection budget reserves its final 100 ms for cooperative cancellation before requesting forced Worker termination; completion waits for its exit. Application exit, recovery exit or restart, and confirmed update installation also cancel collection and wait at most 500 ms for Worker exit. A rejected shutdown cleanup is logged without skipping the remaining cleanup waits. Shutdown prevents late basic-report saves from starting another collector. An update installation failure permits future collection again. Worker messages interrupt collection between bounded records; an in-flight file open, stat, read or close must settle, and synchronous parsing cannot be preempted within one record. The final append uses an abort signal but can leave partial bytes. Forced termination remains the fallback when cooperative cleanup does not finish. The basic report remains available independently. Only one collector runs at a time; concurrent reports keep their basic content without an auxiliary section. A rejected termination request does not release that slot until exit is observed. Get diagnostic report can reveal the basic file before the append finishes. The completion marker confirms only that collection ended, not that all operations were captured; queued bytes and omission counters describe missing material. See [local verification](../../tests/README.md#verification-diagnostics) for fault setup and acceptance steps, and the [Desktop README](../../README.md) for the application overview and development entry points.

--- description: "排查 Desktop 故障或收集报告时阅读，了解恢复操作、报告内容、操作历史和退出限制。" --- # Desktop 故障恢复与诊断 [English](README.md) | 中文 ## 概述 本参考文档说明 Desktop 的原生故障恢复、诊断报告、近期插件操作记录，以及采集和退出时的限制。 ## 目录 - [遇到故障怎么办](#recovery) - [报告包含什么](#report-contents) - [近期操作记录](#operation-records) - [采集与退出行为](#collection-and-shutdown) ## 遇到故障怎么办 主窗口创建、主文档加载、preload、渲染器、Web 初始化或后端的致命失败，会在每个应用进程中打开一次原生恢复对话框。对话框显示首次错误末尾的限长摘要，标明截断情况，并提供“退出”“重启”“禁用第三方插件、备份 profile patch 并重启”，以及报告仍在保存或已保存时的“获取诊断报告”。启动失败保留 Web 加载页和动画；运行中失败保留当前页面。预期关闭、取消导航和普通请求错误不会触发恢复。共享 Web 插件管理器报告包操作错误；插件变更后的 Host 启动失败会进入原生恢复。不通过启动超时推断故障。包含 `listen EADDRINUSE` 的监听失败以退出其他正在运行的 DSH 实例的提示替代诊断和重装建议，提供“退出”“重启”，以及报告仍在保存或已保存时的“获取诊断报告”。 Host 设置可用前，恢复对话框使用本地缓存中最后确认的 Desktop 语言；缓存不存在或无效时回退到系统语言。 恢复操作等待 Host 关闭后才修改插件启用状态。原生恢复操作在 profile 事务锁内调用共享 app-boot 恢复函数。它禁用第三方 bundle，并将 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 重命名为 `cordis.patch.yml.bak-`（重名时追加序号），无需解析；下次启动创建空 patch。已安装包和已有备份保留。home 级 patch 不变。Electron 控制台记录备份路径（或原文件不存在）以及 home 级 patch 未修改。profile 数据无效、重命名失败或写入失败会作为恢复操作错误报告；已完成的修改保留，Desktop 不会假装恢复成功后重启。Desktop 不提供 profile 重置操作或应急 HTML 文档。 ## 报告包含什么 原生弹窗详情最多包含 1,200 个 UTF-16 代码单元和八行诊断，并附上崩溃报告路径或仍在保存、无法保存的状态。获取仍在保存或无法保存的报告时，保留恢复操作失败的标题和详情。配置路径和启动条目排在组合清单之前，避免输出截断时被插件记录挤掉。Host 错误诊断仅保留 stderr 输出的最后 64 Ki 个字符。更早的输出会被丢弃，避免长期运行的 Host 使壳的诊断缓冲区无限增长。 首个致命弹窗打开前，Electron 会向平台日志目录（`app.getPath('logs')`：macOS 为 `~/Library/Logs/iPolloWork`，Windows 与 Linux 为应用 `userData` 目录下的 `logs`）写入一份崩溃报告，最多等待写入一秒；写入缓慢或失败时明确显示仍在保存或无法保存。“获取诊断报告”检查同一次写入，并在系统文件管理器中定位已保存的文件，不停止 Host 或重启；超过首次等待期限后写入完成的文件仍可获取。用户可将文件作为工单附件。附件只包含最初的故障；后续恢复操作错误保留在对话框中，需要另行截图。获取已保存报告会显示分享或打开失败的标题，同时保留恢复错误详情。写入失败时隐藏获取报告按钮，并提示提供窗口截图。 文件 `crash--.log` 记录来源（`host` 为 Host 退出、`web-boot` 为渲染进程启动失败、`renderer` 为渲染进程或文档失败、`main` 为壳自身错误）、后端是否已就绪、应用与运行时版本、包含可枚举属性与 cause 链的错误（截至 256 KiB）、Host 在退出前通过 IPC 报告启动失败时的错误及显式选择的启动元数据（最多 64 Ki 个字符，包含截断提示；启动错误的原始错误文本和启动条目详情分别限制为 8 Ki 个字符，并明确标注截断，为结构化元数据保留空间），以及主窗口最近的 error 级 console 输出（最多 64 KiB）。 因此 Host 退出报告包含保留的 stderr 尾部，其中可能含有插件输出。关闭过程中的致命失败只写报告、不弹窗。平台支持时文件仅所有者可读；启动时保留最新十份报告并删除更早的，不触碰目录中的其他文件。 ## 近期操作记录 操作记录目录与应用单实例锁均按 `userData` 隔离；共享平台日志目录不用于保存操作记录。读取器只读取 `userData/plugin-operations` 下的两个操作记录文件。修复未写完的尾行时保留当前段的完整行与上一段。 版本豁免变更复用 bundle 启停记录字段。豁免版本与安装版本相同时，记录无法区分豁免变更与 bundle 开关。 Host 的 `transportDropped` 只表示最近一次成功发送时的计数下界；Desktop 拒绝的非法或运行 ID 不匹配记录不计入该值。 操作历史保留两个 256 KiB 文件段，单条记录不超过 4 KiB，排队写入不超过 64 KiB。 退出、恢复重启和安装准备最多等待排队写入 500 ms；超时会停用后续写入，此后的排空调用立即返回，不会再次等待；但已经发出的操作系统请求仍可能随后结束。 记录覆盖 Host 启动后观察到的管理器操作，不包含直接执行的 CLI 命令或手工文件修改。包管理器输出保留在原有详细日志中，不复制到摘要。缺失记录、只有开始没有结束的操作以及损坏的历史，都不能说明操作已成功。此收集不诊断内核卡死、OOM 或原生崩溃。 持久化失败也会在本次壳生命周期内停用写入，包括恢复或安装器失败后继续运行的情况，以限制重复失败的 I/O，并避免在可能残缺的写入后追加记录。重启应用会创建新写入器。遗漏和修复计数仅覆盖当前壳生命周期。保留文件段提供比报告附件更大的本地排障历史窗口。 ## 采集与退出行为 基本报告保存后，壳会尝试通过独立 Worker 追加近期插件管理记录；该 Worker 以 `lib/operation-report-worker.js` 打包在 `app.asar` 中。完成标记和遗漏计数用于区分已完成收集与缺失或不完整的材料。 Host 在加载 profile 前报告运行 ID；Host 错误中的 `hostRunId` 与该次运行的操作记录使用同一标识。在此通知之前发生的失败，其运行标识仍为未知。近期操作只是上下文，不是因果证据。 收集只读取 `userData/plugin-operations` 下归其管理的两个文件，最多读取 64 KiB 和 100 条记录；完整追加内容不超过 64 KiB。 500 ms 收集预算中的最后 100 ms 用于协作取消，随后才请求强制终止 Worker；只有 Worker 退出后才确认收集结束。应用退出、恢复退出或重启、确认安装更新也会取消收集，并最多等待 500 ms 确认 Worker 退出。退出清理中的拒绝会被记录，但不会跳过其他清理等待。退出过程中，延迟保存完成的基本报告不会再启动收集器。更新安装失败后可再次收集。 Worker 在有界记录之间处理取消消息；已经发出的文件打开、状态读取、读取或关闭操作必须等待完成，单条记录的同步解析不能被抢占。最后的追加写入传入取消信号，但仍可能留下部分字节。协作清理未及时完成时仍需强制终止。 基本报告独立可用。同时只运行一个收集器；并发报告保留基本内容，不追加辅助部分。终止请求被拒绝时，必须观察到退出才能释放该名额。“获取诊断报告”可能在追加完成前定位基本文件。完成标记仅表示收集结束，不表示捕获了全部操作；排队字节数和遗漏计数说明缺失材料。 故障构造与验收步骤见[本地验证](../../tests/README.zh.md#verification-diagnostics)；应用概览与开发入口见 [Desktop README](../../README.zh.md)。

--- description: "Operate retained Desktop package publication from dedicated macOS and Windows runners." --- # Desktop CI publication English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Publish a completed package from its original machine without downloading its installer again. Both test and production publish binaries followed by update YAML. Both deployments require GitHub Environment approval; only production creates a GitHub App tag. Real COS, CDN and administrator-permission acceptance remain deployment checks; local fixtures do not establish those permissions. ## Table of Contents - [Setup sequence](#setup-sequence) - [Runner labels and queue diagnosis](#runner-labels) - [Machine setup](#machine-setup) - [Package and publish](#package-and-publish) - [Rollout and website publication](#rollout-and-website-publication) - [Recovery and records](#recovery-and-records) - [Restore a channel](#restore-a-channel) ## Setup sequence Use this sequence when onboarding a dedicated machine. The deployment operator owns registration, credentials, approvals and real upload acceptance; repository checks do not establish that a machine can publish. 1. Prepare a runner-owned checkout and an external configuration directory. Follow [Windows machine setup and signing](../../windows-signing/README.md#machine-setup) or [macOS runner and signing setup](../../packaging/README.md#macos-actions) for tools, templates and platform credentials. 2. Register the runner using GitHub **Settings → Actions → Runners**, or the organization's runner administration page. Record its exact registered name, grant this repository access to its runner group, and assign the [required labels](#runner-labels). Keep the default labels during registration. 3. Install and start the platform supervisor described in the platform guide. Windows Task Scheduler and the macOS LaunchAgent require the configured user's login; they do not provide unattended startup before login. Confirm both GitHub connectivity and `Listening for Jobs`, then check the runner is online in GitHub. 4. Complete [machine publication configuration](#machine-setup), the repository's `DESKTOP_PUBLISH_RUNNERS` variable, and the two deployment Environments. The repository administrator owns routing and reviewers; the COS administrator owns bucket configuration and object read/write permissions; production also needs the configured GitHub App. 5. Run a signed Windows or notarized macOS **test** package using [Package and publish](#package-and-publish). Confirm the packaging job used the intended registered runner and retained its files. Dispatch publication from `main` with that run ID and attempt; confirm `prepare` actually starts on the same machine and produces the approval summary. 6. Inspect the summary's environment, version, channel and URLs before approving the test upload. Verify the publication record, public installer download and update feed. Test acceptance does not establish production permissions: provision and approve production separately. Keep the run/attempt and acceptance results for recovery. ## Runner labels and queue diagnosis GitHub matches every label in a job's `runs-on` list. The [default-label rules](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/self-hosted-runners/use-in-a-workflow) explain why registration with `--no-default-labels` can leave an online runner ineligible. The current workflows require: | Job | Required labels on the same runner | | --- | --- | | Windows packaging | `dsh-win-package-trial` | | macOS packaging | `self-hosted`, `macOS`, `ARM64`, `dsh-mac-package-trial` | | All original-machine publication and rollout jobs | `self-hosted` and the selected `DESKTOP_PUBLISH_RUNNERS` entry's `label` | A runner with only `dsh-win-package-trial` can package Windows but cannot accept publication. Its routing entry does not add labels to its GitHub registration. Have a runner administrator correct the registered labels; changing the route's `target` or restarting a healthy listener does not supply a missing label. For a queued job, compare the job page's requested labels with **Settings → Actions → Runners**, then check repository/group access and whether the matching runner is online and idle. A running supervisor only establishes that its process exists. A successful hosted `route` job only establishes package selection; it does not establish that `prepare` can be assigned. A deployment waiting for approval needs its Environment reviewer, while an assigned job that fails needs its step logs. Diagnose these states separately before restarting anything. ## Machine setup Keep `DSH_PACKAGING_CONFIG_DIR` pointed at the existing machine packaging directory. Completed attempts are copied to its sibling `releases///`; `DSH_DESKTOP_RELEASES_DIR` overrides that root with an absolute path. The inventory includes installers, update archives, blockmaps, completion metadata and a credential-free manifest. Debug packages are retained but cannot publish. Copies are checked before the attempt directory becomes visible, and an existing attempt cannot be replaced. GitHub retains the same file inventory for 14 days. Local files remain until an operator removes them; do not delete an attempt while it is being verified or published. Start from the [macOS test](../../config/publishing/macos/test.json.example), [macOS production](../../config/publishing/macos/production.json.example), [Windows test](../../config/publishing/windows/test.json.example), or [Windows production](../../config/publishing/windows/production.json.example) template. Create the `publishing/` directory and copy the selected file to `publishing/.json` below `DSH_PACKAGING_CONFIG_DIR`. Replace the example bucket, test origin, absolute paths, macOS signing identity and team ID or Windows certificate thumbprint, and production App client ID with the machine settings; keep the fixed production origin. Templates contain no credentials and do not grant COS, GitHub, or signing permissions. Store referenced secrets outside Git with access restricted to the publishing account. macOS uses the same configuration for arm64 and x64; the retained package determines the target. Each configuration declares `bucket`, HTTPS `origin` without a path, and an absolute `credentialsFile`. The credential file contains only `secretId` and `secretKey`. macOS also requires `macOS.signingIdentity` and `macOS.teamId`; Windows requires `windows.certificateThumbprint`. Production requires the exact origin `https://download.deepseek.com` and `githubApp.clientId` plus an absolute `githubApp.privateKeyFile`. The uploader supports permanent COS credentials, not STS session credentials. Administrators must keep test and production buckets unversioned (neither enabled nor suspended). Publication assumes this deployment prerequisite and does not call `GetBucketVersioning` or require its permission. Immutable binary PUTs retain `x-cos-forbid-overwrite`; their protection depends on administrators maintaining the bucket configuration. Set the repository variable `DESKTOP_PUBLISH_RUNNERS` to a JSON mapping of registered runner names to unique labels and targets, for example `{"mini":{"label":"dsh-mini-publish","target":["mac-arm64","mac-x64"]}}`. Assign that label to exactly that runner. A target may be a single name or a nonempty list; the Mac entry above authorizes both packaging workflows on the same machine. Windows uses target `win-x64`. The retained target must match the selected packaging workflow. The routing job checks the original successful job, and the publisher checks its own runner name against the recorded name. Machines need no shared filesystem or LAN connection to each other. An administrator must create `desktop-test` and `desktop-production`, each with required reviewers and an allowed `main` deployment branch. The workflow checks reviewers for either deployment. Test can allow self-approval. The GitHub App needs installation access to this repository and Contents write permission, plus permission under the `desktop-v*` tag ruleset to create release tags. Reviewer approval does not transfer the reviewer's tag permissions to the App. Missing configuration stops publication; there is no personal-token fallback. The App action creates and later revokes a short-lived token. Protect the local private key and COS credential files with the publishing account's filesystem permissions. The token action accepts key contents, so the masked PEM also passes through the runner's temporary `GITHUB_OUTPUT` file during the job; masking hides logs, not local file access. Environment approval gates this workflow, not arbitrary code running under the same machine account. Account isolation and forced source-branch restrictions are separate operational work. Keep existing release Environments unchanged. The test job uses its own reviewers and never creates a real release tag; local simulated transports exercise tag creation and recovery without verifying App permissions. ## Package and publish The publication form accepts an optional `staging_percentage` integer from 0 to 100. It applies to the retained package’s channel (nightly or stable), appears in the approval summary, and is included in the published YAML and audit record without modifying retained artifacts. Leave it blank for the packaged default (normally full rollout). Completed publications cannot change this percentage through a retry; same-version feed conflicts remain errors. For publication to either test or production, choose Windows `signing=signed` or leave macOS **Skip notarization** unchecked. Unsigned and unnotarized packages are only for internal debugging; they cannot publish or provide automatic updates. Before installing dependencies, the hosted routing job rejects debugging artifacts identified by the selected run and attempt. An archive-only rerun retains the original build attempt in artifact names, so this early check can miss it; local manifest qualification still rejects debugging builds before publication. Missing artifact metadata does not establish eligibility: the original machine still validates its retained manifest and signatures. A debugging-package rejection requires a new signed/notarized package and its run ID / attempt; retrying publication cannot qualify the existing bytes. Select the platform's `Package Desktop` workflow, preset, source, channel and version mode. `source_ref` accepts repository branch names (for example `feature/desktop-update`) or `dsh-v*` tags for test; production accepts only `main` or `dsh-v*` tags. Names matching `dsh-v` followed by a digit and letters, digits, dots or hyphens are treated as tags, even if a branch has that name. Tags must match the selected product version. We recommend dispatching the packaging workflow from `main` and enter the source separately; raw commit SHAs, PR refs and fork repositories are not supported. Sources without the CI adapters fail before dependency installation. Only select trusted branches: their build code runs on the signing machine. This is an operating convention, not enforced workflow-origin or credential isolation. Publication uses the recorded commit and requires it to remain in the selected branch history; normal branch advances are allowed, deletion or a diverging force-push rejects. Tag publication requires the tag to still resolve to the recorded commit. Dispatch the publisher from `main`; its hosted routing job rejects other refs before scheduling the original machine. The packaged source commit is recorded separately. `version_mode=default` selects follow-dsh for production and build-number for test; follow-dsh preserves the selected checkout’s dsh version, build-number appends date/run/attempt in either environment, and manual requires `build_version`. Existing dispatch commands using `-f version_mode=auto` must use `-f version_mode=build-number`, and `-f version_mode=product` becomes `-f version_mode=follow-dsh`; the local CLI option `--build-version auto` is unchanged. Workflows temporarily pass legacy mode names to sources that contain the CI adapters but predate the mode rename; current parsers accept both names. Removal is planned for 2027-01-04, not automatic: remove workflow mappings and parser aliases together, then require selected sources to support the new mode names. The operator-selected channel accepts any supported build version, including alpha and RC versions; it does not change version precedence or permit client downgrades. The optional `test_release_id` is the test URL prefix: blank retains the machine default, successive upgrade tests on that platform need the same value, and defaults should be rotated periodically. It is not a GitHub run ID. See [packaging configuration](../../packaging/README.md#configuration-and-local-builds) for its validation and rotation limits. Packaging only retains files. After success, open **Publish Desktop · COS → Run workflow** on `main`, enter `package_run_id` from the packaging run URL, and optionally enter `package_run_attempt`. Blank selects the latest attempt and its successful package job. An archival-only retry retains the original build attempt; a failed newer package job never falls back to an older success. An explicit attempt selects that build even when its separate GitHub archival failed. Windows must be signed; macOS must finish notarization and stapling.
